p: We are taught that a good brand looks polished, with a clean logo, a tidy shelf and matching colours.
[[Polish is easy to buy]], so it proves very little about whether anyone will return.
Near an old city market, a sweet shop has a hand-painted board with one letter faded.
A queue forms outside it every evening, while [[the glass-front bakery]] next door stays quiet.
The brands I have seen last longest were easy to describe to a friend in one sentence.
[[The look]] usually arrived after that, and rarely decided anything.
A brand audit scores logos, colours and consistency, because those are easy to measure.
[[Trust builds slowly]] through habit, and habit is hard to put in a score.

slides.setup: Before paying for a new logo, ask yourself
slides.follow: That answer is worth more than a new typeface.

p: At six in the evening the faded board is lit by a single bulb.
[[The queue]] is already around the corner.
